21.issue_summary: App declares READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=32), WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE (maxSdkVersion=28), and uses requestLegacyExternalStorage=true, but all file operations use Capacitor Filesystem plugin with Directory.Documents (scoped storage on API 30+). No raw file path access found. The permissions are legacy artifacts from pre-scoped-storage era.
21.evidence: Manifest: requestLegacyExternalStorage=true at line 11, WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 55 (maxSdkVersion=28), READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE at line 57 (maxSdkVersion=32). main.tsx:31 creates 'Biz-flow/' folder via Capacitor Filesystem mkdir(Directory.Documents). nativeFileService.ts writes/reads PDFs via Capacitor Filesystem to Directory.Documents/Biz-flow/. DocumentShareModal.tsx and useDocumentActions.ts similarly use Capacitor Filesystem scoped API. No direct Environment.getExternalStorageDirectory() usage anywhere in the codebase. localStorage reference in assets is browser-level web storage, unrelated to Android file permissions.
21.recommendation: Remove READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE from AndroidManifest.xml. Remove android:requestLegacyStorage="true" (only applies to API 29, irrelevant on targetSdk=35). The Capacitor Filesystem plugin already uses scoped storage via the SAF on API 30+ and works correctly without these permissions.

22.issue_summary: Login screen detected. The app implements a full authentication flow with email/password sign-in, sign-up, password reset, and Google OAuth, gating features behind a user account.
22.evidence: AuthPage.tsx (lines 60-207) renders a full login/signup/reset UI with email/password form and Google Sign-In button. ConnectAccountModal.tsx (lines 76-182) provides an in-app modal for account connection with Supabase. AuthContext.tsx (lines 40-145) manages auth state and exposes signIn, signUp, signOut, resetPassword, signInWithGoogle. AuthService.ts (lines 13-62) implements actual Supabase Auth API calls (signInWithPassword, signUp, signOut, signInWithOAuth). Users can register and authenticate via email/password or Google.
22.recommendation: Administrative Console Requirements: Because your app implements a login flow, you MUST complete two manual setup steps in the Play Console dashboard: (1) Submit active, non-expiring test credentials so Google Play reviewers can access gated features. (2) Submit a public-facing web link for account deletion to satisfy Google Play's data deletion policies.

23.issue_summary: App handles user accounts via Supabase Auth but NO in-app account deletion mechanism exists. The signOut() method only clears the local session without deleting the remote user record.
23.evidence: AuthContext.tsx lines 99-104: signOut() only calls supabase.auth.signOut() and clears local state (setState({ user: null })) — it does NOT perform a remote account deletion or send a delete/purge API call. AuthService.ts lines 38-42: signOut() calls supabase.auth.signOut() and logs warnings but never triggers account deletion. No file in the codebase contains any account deletion code (searched for 'deleteAccount', 'delete_account', 'apagar.conta', 'removeAccount', 'deletar', 'remove account'). No Profile or Settings pages exist where a deletion option could be placed.
23.recommendation: Implement in-app deletion: Create a highly discoverable path (e.g., under User Profile / Account Settings) to let users initiate account deletion directly in the app. The deletion must call a Supabase Admin API or Edge Function to permanently remove the user's remote database records, not merely sign them out.
